sections.heading: Overview of the Present Tense
paragraphs: In Hungarian, the present tense (jelen idő) is used to talk about actions happening now, habits, and general facts. Verbs change their endings depending on the subject and whether the object is definite or indefinite.
*The Hungarian present tense can correspond to the English simple present, present continuous, present perfect, and even future tense.*

sections.heading: Indefinite vs. Definite Conjugation
paragraphs: Hungarian verbs have two conjugation types: indefinite and definite.
Indefinite conjugation is used when the object is unknown, general, or not mentioned.
Definite conjugation is used when the object is specific and known.
list: Indefinite example: Minden nap olvasok. (I read every day.)
Definite example: Olvasom a könyvet. (I read the book.)

sections.heading: Questions | Indefinite
paragraphs: Questions are formed simply by using rising intonation or adding a question mark—no extra auxiliary verb is needed.

sections.heading: Examples
list: Én tanulom a leckét. – I study the lesson (specific object).
Mi tanulunk minden nap. – We study every day.
Mi tanuljuk az új szavakat. – We study the new words.

sections.heading: Important Points
list: Indefinite is used when the object is absent, unspecified, or general.
Definite is used when the object is specific or known (e.g., a könyvet, az új leckét).
Negatives are formed by adding *nem* before the verb.
Questions rely on intonation or a question mark—Hungarian does not use English-style auxiliaries like “do/does”.
